title: Interstate moves made easy customer information sheet

paragraphs.text: Now turn to section one.
Section one. You will hear a telephone conversation between a representative of a moving company and a customer. First, you have some time to look at questions one to three.
You will see that there is an example that has been done for you. On this occasion only, the conversation relating to this will be played first.
Good morning. Interstate Moves Made Easy. Can I help you?
Yes. My husband is being transferred to Sydney, and I wonder if you could help me find suitable rental accommodation.
Certainly. Now, let me just get a form, and I can get some details. Can you give me your name, please?
Yes, it's Anne Jones.

The customer's name is Anne Jones, so Jones has been written in the space. Now we shall begin. You should answer the questions as you listen because you will not hear the recording a second time. Listen carefully and answer questions one to three.
Good morning. Interstate Moves Made Easy. Can I help you?
Yes. My husband is being transferred to Sydney, and I wonder if you could help me find suitable rental accommodation.
Certainly. Now, let me just get a form, and I can get some details. Can you give me your name, please?
Yes, it's Anne Jones.
And what's your number at home?
Six six two one eight zero four seven.
And do you have a mobile number?
No, but I can give you my work number, zero four two seven one three nine six eight four.
Fine. And you said you were planning to move to Sydney, is that right?
Yes.
Ah, how exciting. It's a lovely city. And where are you living now?
We're out in Western Australia in a place called Somerton.
Can you spell that, please?
Yes. It's S-O-M-E-R-T-O-N.
That's gonna be a big move for you, isn't it?
Yes. Well, we've been here in Western Australia for a few years now, so it seems like a good time to move.
Okay. So it's you, your husband, and any children?
Yes, just one child, Ben. He's two, but he's gonna be 3 next week.
Okay.
Before you hear the rest of the conversation, you have some time to look at questions four to ten.
Now listen and answer questions four to ten.
Right. So let's think about accommodation first of all. What kind of place are you looking for? Presumably something large enough for your whole family.
Yes. We're in a lovely big house at the moment, but I realize we won't be able to afford that in Sydney. So I'd be happy in a flat, but as long as there is enough space.
Yes. I think it's a lot easier to find a flat here at the moment. Do you have any idea what sort of area you'd like to be in?
I prefer the north to the south, but I've heard it's a lot more expensive. Is that right?
Yes, it can be more expensive, but there are some lovely flats there.
Well, that would be my first choice then.
Great. And how many bedrooms do you want?
Well, there are only three of us, but I would like an extra room for visitors and one for an office, so four would be great.
Of course. Now, what about special facilities? Is there anything that you particularly require?
Well, of course we'll miss our big garden, and I realize that is out of the question, but it has to be near a park.
Okay. I'll put that on the form. And is there anything else? What about a shopping center?
I'm not much of a shopper, but we're very keen on keeping fit, and I'm teaching Ben to swim, so a pool would be great. Would that be possible?
Well, it all depends on how much you're prepared to pay, but I'll put it down as one of your requirements anyway. Now, what about rent? How much do you want to spend per week?
What sort of prices are properties like these?
Usually in a region of five hundred dollars and up to one thousand dollars for the really luxurious ones. But I'd say for $650 a week, you could get a really nice flat with everything you want.
Okay. Let's say up to that then.
Great. Now, last of all, when are you planning to move over here?

We're fairly flexible about when we get over there, but we've got to move out of our house by the first of December. We're planning on traveling around a little to visit friends and family, but we would definitely like to move into our new house by 15th December, ready for Christmas.
Right. I'll put that down as your moving date. We can always alter it later. Is there anything else I can do? Obviously, you don't need to find a school yet.
No, but I'd like to fly to Sydney next month on the thirty-first of August to check out some properties.
That's a great idea. Would you like me to book your flight or a hotel for you?
Actually, I've already booked my flight, but we do need a hotel. Somewhere near to the properties would be great. I'll be traveling with Ben, and we'll just stay overnight.
That's fine. I'll organize that as soon as I can. Well, I'll look forward to seeing you soon, and-
